_doc: Revert-verify mutant for c3f586b4 (#4291) — the adapter half. The wiring spec beside this one proves the collaborators are HANDED the shared reader; this one proves the reader is worth sharing, i.e. that a second read of the same file does not reach the disk. Separate spec because the driver mutates ONE subject per run.

M5_content_memo_defeated._note: Semantics are preserved (the base class still raises FileNotFoundError); only the memo goes. S3 reddens because the second read of one file now reaches the disk; S6 because the walks stop sharing reads. S1/S2/S4/S5 stay green — the adapter is still the memoising CLASS and the reader is still handed out, it simply no longer remembers anything.

M8_forget_leaves_content_memo._note: Added after review of this PR: the reviewer removed `this.contents.clear()` from forget() and THREE suites stayed green (create-single-pass 6/6, create-batch 25/25, create unit 19/19). The safety claim it enforces — a write drops every memo — was an invariant of the CALLERS (planning never writes; the write half uses a separate FileSystemVaultAdapter), not of this class. Axis S7 pins it on the class, so a future refactor of forget() that drops the line reddens instead of shipping silently (integration-test-revert-verify §A8).
